issues.legal_issue: A court cannot grant temporary relief as the sole and final relief in a constitutional writ proceeding when it declines to determine the rights on which substantive relief would depend and grants protection only to facilitate a later civil suit.
material_facts: The applicants claimed interests in mining leases and challenged government actions cancelling temporary permits and requiring them to remove their assets.
The High Court expressly declined to decide the parties’ rights, leaving those issues for a contemplated civil suit.

Because a statutory notice period delayed filing that suit, the High Court ordered the government not to disturb the applicants’ possession in the interim, and gave directions for working the mines during that period.
The writ petitions were disposed of without any determination of the underlying rights.
issues.conclusion: The High Court lacked jurisdiction to grant interim protection as the only relief in the writ petitions; its orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Article 226 permits directions for purposes beyond enforcing fundamental rights, but its concluding words must be read in the context of the Article as a whole, and the existence of a right is the foundation for exercising jurisdiction. Interim relief may be granted only in aid of and ancillary to the main relief available upon final determination of rights in a suit or proceeding. A court that declines to determine those rights cannot use Article 226 to grant temporary-injunction-like relief solely to facilitate the filing of a civil suit. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_proceeding and court_declines_to_determine_underlying_rights and temporary_protection_is_only_relief and protection_is_pending_separate_suit

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The applicant brought a proceeding seeking a court order against a public authority through a constitutional writ jurisdiction.
predicates.court_declines_to_determine_underlying_r: The court left undecided the rights on which substantive relief would depend.
predicates.temporary_protection_is_only_relief: The court granted temporary protection without granting or deciding any substantive relief in the proceeding.
predicates.protection_is_pending_separate_suit: The court made the protection effective only while the applicant pursued a separate suit.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ proceeding ends without a decision on underlying rights and grants only temporary protection pending a separate suit, the output is that interim-only relief is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An order disposing of a proceeding is final for purposes of appeal even when its operation is time-limited, if nothing further remains to be done in that proceeding.
material_facts: The High Court disposed of the writ petitions by issuing directions that operated only until a specified time or an earlier event.
The High Court stated that it was not prepared to make any other order on the petitions, and nothing further remained to be decided in them.
An objection was raised that the appeals were not maintainable because the High Court had not made final orders.
issues.conclusion: The orders were final because the petitions had been disposed of and nothing further remained to be done; their limited duration did not make them non-final.
issues.legal_principle: An order is final when it disposes of the proceeding and leaves nothing further to be done in it. Limiting the period during which the order operates does not prevent it from being final. No earlier cases are relied upon.

predicates.appeal_from_disposed_proceeding: A party appealed from an order made in a proceeding that the lower court treated as disposed of.
predicates.nothing_further_remains_in_proceeding: No further decision or action remains for the lower court to take in that proceeding.
predicates.order_has_limited_duration: The order is expressed to operate only for a limited time or until an earlier event.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns an order disposing of a proceeding, nothing remains to be done in that proceeding, and the order has a limited duration, the output is that the order is final for appeal.
